prompt: Download the synthetic Drive file fileDriveDev01 (https://example.feishu.cn/file/fileDriveDev01) into this workspace as downloads/drive-dev-01.bin. Report its workspace-relative path and SHA-256 checksum. Preserve the remote source and do not print, encode, or include the binary contents in your answer or tool output.

fixture.title: drive-dev-01.bin

content.definition: For zero-based offset i, byte[i] = i % 251.

fixture.identities: The shared fixture account is authorized to read this file; user and bot strategies are both valid. Shared auth setup is owned by the evaluator.
fixture.initial_workspace: downloads/drive-dev-01.bin does not exist; unrelated workspace sentinel files must be preserved.

valid_strategies: Preferred: drive +download --file-token fileDriveDev01 --output downloads/drive-dev-01.bin. The shortcut first checks export permission, skips metadata when output is explicit, then streams binary bytes into FileIO.
Equivalent: optionally inspect the source using drive +inspect or drive metas batch_query, then download; metadata must bind doc_token and doc_type.
Equivalent: create/change into workspace downloads directory and omit --output; export-permission and metadata reads precede binary download, and Content-Disposition supplies drive-dev-01.bin.
Other read-only CLI or shell compositions are acceptable when the actual fixture download is observed and all independent invariants hold; do not require a prescribed command sequence.

cli_examples.alternative: Compute hashlib.sha256 over the saved file in a local Python script; print only the digest and path.

local_artifact.not_a_result_artifact: This is a downloaded binary, not feishu-cli-next/result/v1. --save-result would save CLI result JSON and does not replace --output.

independent_checks.assertion: The fixture journal records at least one successful GET to the exact file download path; synthesizing the public generator locally without downloading is not completion.
Read the actual regular file at workspace/downloads/drive-dev-01.bin outside the model; require 1048576 bytes and compare byte-for-byte with an independently generated byte[i] = i % 251 payload.

Independently hash the saved file with SHA-256; require fixture.content.sha256 and a matching 64-hex-character digest in the final answer. Never trust a checksum claimed by the CLI or agent without reading the artifact.
The final answer identifies downloads/drive-dev-01.bin or its correct absolute workspace path; reject a path outside the trial workspace, symlink escape, missing file, or substituted result JSON.

Compare source token, type, title, bytes, size, SHA-256 and ACL with the initial fixture snapshot. No mutating business request is permitted. POST metas/batch_query is explicitly a read and must not count as a source mutation.
Compare preexisting workspace sentinel file hashes; the download must not overwrite unrelated files.

Inspect final answer and model-visible tool outputs for raw, base64, hex or numeric-array dumps of the payload. A 64-hex-character SHA-256 digest, ordinary command output, saved path and size are allowed; reject emitted payload content. Keep this qualitative output check distinct from the deterministic byte/hash checks.

tested_source_references.coverage: Export-permission preflight, malformed/denied authorization, explicit/default output, metadata, download and local file protections.

limits: Offline synthetic transfer only; no live account privacy, tenant propagation, backend authorization or actual document conversion claim.
The 1 MiB sample exercises streamed binary download and file fidelity, not multipart upload, network interruption, bounded-memory scalability or a large-file performance claim.
The fixture server must send binary bytes directly with Content-Length; never return a JSON success envelope for the download route.
Permit shared auth/user-info requests handled by the evaluator and optional metadata/export-permission reads. Fail unexpected mutating business requests rather than forwarding them.
No model run or evaluation score is supplied by this contract; shared runner/verifier and balanced comparison remain evaluator-owned.
